title: She leads a global fight against violence toward women. In 2026, she became only the second South Asian in the National Women's Hall of Fame.

sources.text: Equality Now - Mona Sinha, CEO of Equality Now, inducted into National Women's Hall of Fame
India Weekly - Equality Now CEO Sharmila Mona Sinha Becomes 2nd Indian-Origin Woman in National Women's Hall of Fame

caption:
She leads a global fight against violence toward women. In 2026, she became only the second South Asian in the National Women's Hall of Fame.

The ceremony, held at the George Eastman Museum in Rochester, NY, recognized more than 40 years of her leadership in gender equality, philanthropy and advocacy. She is only the second South Asian ever inducted, after Indra Nooyi - joining a roster that includes Michelle Obama, Rosa Parks and Janet Yellen.

Those legal reforms against discrimination and violence toward women and girls are estimated to have benefited 69 million women and girls - concrete policy change, not symbolic advocacy.

Sinha's induction marks an Indian-origin leader influencing international law on women's rights at the highest level - a different kind of global Indian success story than the ones usually celebrated.
